Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the VitaHealth Partners Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not place your line on hold, as background noise may be transmitted. Today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss VitaHealth Partners' financial results for the second quarter of 2024. Joining me on the call are Dr. Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Emily Patel, Chief Medical Officer; and Tom Hargrove, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Michael Reynolds.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the second quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency as a leading integrated healthcare delivery system with over 120 acute care hospitals, 250 ambulatory surgery centers, and a growing post-acute network across 28 states, primarily in the Southeast, Midwest, and Southwest.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on five key aspects: operating margin by segment, initiatives to improve operating margin, factors affecting operating margin, total admissions and patient days, and an overview of key financial performance highlights.

In terms of operating margins by segment, we saw strong performance across the board, reflecting the resilience of our diversified model amid labor inflation, supply chain volatility, and CMS pressures. Our acute care hospitals, ambulatory services, post-acute care, and international operations all contributed to consolidated adjusted operating margin expansion.

On initiatives to improve operating margins, we're advancing our multi-faceted efforts through supply chain optimization, labor productivity, revenue cycle enhancements, and clinical efficiencies, targeting sustainable gains toward our long-term goals.

Factors influencing these margins include robust revenue growth from volumes, case mix, and payer dynamics, coupled with disciplined cost controls in labor and supplies.

Volume-wise, total admissions and patient days showed solid year-over-year and sequential increases, driven by elective recoveries and high-acuity service lines.

Finally, our key financial highlights underscore same-facility growth, EBITDA expansion, and strong cash flows.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to Lisa to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Michael, and good morning, everyone. As Michael mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Net revenue for the second quarter was $3.9 billion, an increase of 9% compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, improved case mix index, and favorable payer mix dynamics.

Let me dive deeper into these areas, starting with an overview of our key financial performance highlights. As a leading operator of acute care hospitals and outpatient facilities, our results reflect same-facility growth, disciplined cost management, and execution in high-growth markets. Consolidated net revenues reached this $3.9 billion figure, up 9% year-over-year, with same-facility net revenue growing 7%, driven by volume expansion, pricing leverage, and payer shifts. Admissions totaled around 285,000 equivalent admissions, up 6% year-over-year, with patient days increasing 5%. Case mix index improved to 1.85 from 1.79, highlighting a shift to higher-acuity cases like orthopedics, cardiology, and oncology. Net revenue per admission rose 3% to about $14,700, supported by commercial pricing uplifts and steady Medicare reimbursements post-CMS updates. Outpatient revenue, now over half of total, grew 12%, propelled by ambulatory surgery centers where volumes surged 15%.

Adjusted EBITDA came in at $825 million, up 12% year-over-year, delivering a 19.7% margin—our highest Q3 in five years and 110 basis points above last year, marking the 10th straight quarter of expansion. Same-facility EBITDA grew 10%, with operating leverage from revenues outpacing expenses. Labor costs improved to 46% of revenue through workforce optimization, dropping RN contract labor to 4% via float pools and agency partnerships. Supply costs fell 50 basis points to 13.5% with GPO savings on implants and stents totaling $45 million. Net income was $450 million, or $1.85 diluted EPS, up 15%, with adjusted EPS at $2.10 beating consensus. Cash flow from operations hit $950 million, adjusted free cash flow $650 million after $300 million CapEx. We repurchased $400 million in shares and maintain net debt at $12.5 billion with a strong 3.8x levered multiple.

Regionally, the Southeast led with 12% same-facility growth in Florida and Texas, EBITDA margins at 22%. Midwest saw 6% growth, West/Northeast 4%. Investments in revenue cycle modernization improved days in A/R to 48 and captured $120 million in claims.

Turning to operating margin by segment, our consolidated adjusted operating margin was 7.2% for the quarter, up 110 basis points year-over-year from 6.1% and 40 basis points sequentially from Q1's 6.8%—our strongest since Q4 2021, driven by 320 basis points of case mix index lift to 1.92, labor productivity, and our AI-powered revenue cycle platform with Change Healthcare. Excluding COVID stimulus, this is a record.

Acute care hospitals, 72% of revenue at $2.8 billion, delivered 5.4% margins, up 180 basis points YoY and flat sequentially. Volumes included 2.3% surgical growth to 145,000 cases, high-acuity orthopedics and cardiology with da Vinci Xi in 85% of ORs. CMI up 4% YoY to outpace national averages, commercial payers at 58%. Southeast at 6.8% margins with low agency nurse use at 8%; Midwest 4.9%, offset by telehealth reducing readmissions 15%. Supply costs down 7% per case via Vizient GPO.

Ambulatory services, 15% of revenue at $580 million, hit 18.7% margins, up 250 basis points YoY. ASC procedure volumes up 12% to 420,000, musculoskeletal and GI leading. Site-of-care shift captured 28% of surgical volume. Southwest at 21.2% with Medicare updates and bundled contracts at 105% reimbursement. Nuance documentation cut coding backlogs 40%, net revenue at 98%. Adding 25 ASCs targeting 25% ROIC.

Post-acute care, 10% at $390 million, improved to 12.1%, up 140 basis points YoY. Home health and hospice up 9%, STAR ratings at 4.2 for PDGM. Texas at 14.5%, Midwest mitigated shortages. $150 million in value-based pilots with Humana targeting 15% margins, shifting 30% discharges to home health.

International, 3% at $115 million, 14.3% margins. India JV at 16.8% on 18% growth from medical tourism; UK at 10.2%, countered Brexit tariffs with local sourcing down 25%.

We expect 7.8% consolidated margins in Q3, with $200 million synergies from procurement and Oracle Cerner migration. Risks like labor strikes and opioid settlements, but 42% EBITDA debt coverage.

Now, on initiatives to improve operating margins, we're pursuing our Margin Resilience Framework for 15-17% by 2026, with $150 million run-rate savings year-to-date. Adjusted EBITDA was $285 million on $2.4 billion revenue, margin at 12.5%, up 220 basis points.

Supply chain: Consolidated GPO to Vizient for 85% of $450 million spend, 9% reductions, 14% on joint kits. RFID inventory cut stockouts 35%, waste 22%, adding 40 basis points, impactful in Southeast.

Labor: FlexCare AI scheduling to 1:4.8 ratios, agency down 28% or $45 million, CNA upskilling cut premium pay to 12%. Midwest margins up 150 basis points. CMI to 1.85.

RCM: $20 million Waystar and Epic overhaul, denials to 8.2%, AR days to 42. Renegotiated contracts for 5-7% uplifts, Medicare Advantage to 28%, net revenue per admission to $14,200, 90 basis points lift. Bundled pilots in rural sites to 11% margins.

Clinical efficiency: Amwell telehealth cut readmissions 18%, ALOS to 4.2. ASCs at 22% volume, 28% margins. ClosedLoop AI for 92% bed forecast, OR to 88%.

Integrated dashboard tracks KPIs; Southeast/Southwest at 14.5%, Northeast 10.8%. Moderating inflation, CapEx $300 million for 200-300 bps accretion, on track for 13.8% full-year.

Key factors affecting operating margin expanded it to 12.8%, up 160 basis points YoY and 50 sequentially. Revenue grew 9.2% to $2.45 billion, above industry 6.8%.

Volumes: Admissions up 4.5%, electives 7%, orthopedics 12%, cardiology 9%; outpatient 6.2%, ASCs 15%. Southeast +6.1%.

CMI to 1.92, +2.7%, high-acuity robotics adding 120 basis points.

Payer mix: Commercial 52%, rates +4.1%; Medicare 28%. Denials to 8.2%, revenue per admission +4.6% to $14,200. Midwest softer at 2.8% from Medicaid.

Expenses up 7.1% to $2.14 billion, below guidance. Labor 52.3% flat, contract to 4.2% down 35% sequential via Apex Flex AI to 94% fill rates, premium pay -22%.

Supplies 22.1%, +9.4%, offset by 8% GPO savings $28 million, OR 78%.

Bad debt to 3.1%, Epic collections +18%.

EHR Epic Hyperdrive +3% capture, GHX savings 7%. ASC growth to 40, 20% margins; ACO-REACH $15 million. M&A accretive.

Q3 margins 12.5-13.0%, full-year raised to 12.2-12.6%.

On volumes, total admissions were 52,300, up 6.8% YoY from 48,950 and 2.4% QoQ from 51,080. Patient days 292,150, +8.2% YoY from 270,100, +2.1% QoQ from 286,200. ALOS 5.59 days, up 13 basis points YoY.

YoY admissions outpaced peers with 12% ortho, 9% oncology, 7% cardiac. Patient days amplified by acuity, CMI 1.82 +2.5%.

QoQ solid, ASC shifts. Southeast 75% growth, Florida +9.2%; Texas offset uncompensated; Midwest +4.1%, neuro +10%.

Epic MyChart -18% delays, telehealth +25%. Q3 admissions 5-7%, days 6-8%, margins +150 bps to 28%.

Our operating expenses were $3.4 billion, representing 87% of net revenue. We're managing costs while investing in growth, particularly supply chain and labor optimization. Net income was $450 million, or $1.85 per share. We're pleased and confident in our goals.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Emily Patel for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Emily Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. Good morning. We are making significant progress in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our precision oncology and critical care programs have shown promising results, with readmission rates down 15-18% through telehealth and bundled care. Our Epic MyChart and Amwell integrations have enhanced patient experience, reducing ALOS and improving care coordination with AI forecasting and robotic precision in ORs. STAR ratings at 4.2 support reimbursements, and we're expanding value-based pilots.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Michael.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Emily. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to ask a question, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Our first question comes from David Miller with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Miller:
Good morning. Can you provide more detail on the impact of the AI-powered revenue cycle management platform on your revenue growth and the impact on hospital efficiency?

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Good morning, David. The AI platform with Change Healthcare has been transformative, contributing to our 320 basis point CMI lift and denial reductions from 14% to 8.2%, directly boosting net revenue realization to 98% and adding 90 basis points to margins. On efficiency, it slashed coding backlogs 40%, AR days to 42, and supported labor productivity, enabling OR utilization to 88%. Full-quarter ramp drove record margins excluding stimulus.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Klein with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Sarah Klein:
What are your plans for expanding your network of hospitals and clinics in the coming year?

Tom Hargrove:
Thanks, Sarah. We're targeting 25 greenfield ASCs and bolt-on M&A like our recent Texas tuck-ins, focusing on high-ROIC ortho and GI in Southeast and Southwest. De novo ASCs project 25% ROIC in 18 months, shifting 30% volumes outpatient for 20-28% margins. CapEx $300-450 million supports 40 ASCs by year-end, leveraging site-neutrality and population growth in Florida, Texas MSAs.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Thompson with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mike Thompson:
Can you elaborate on the specific technologies you are implementing to improve care coordination?

Dr. Emily Patel:
Absolutely, Mike. Key is Epic MyChart and Hyperdrive for 90% rollout, reducing admission delays 18% and coding errors 15%. Amwell telehealth cuts CHF readmissions 18%, ClosedLoop AI forecasts beds 92% accurately. Nuance Dragon for documentation, Optum navigation for post-acute STAR 4.2. Telestroke and STEMI networks boost neuro/cardiac, with da Vinci Xi in 85% ORs enhancing acuity and outcomes below national readmission benchmarks.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong:
Thanks. On the post-acute margins, how are the value-based pilots progressing and any update on international growth?

Lisa Chen:
Hi Lisa. Post-acute hit 12.1%, with Humana pilots shifting 30% discharges home, targeting 15%. $150 million investment yielding 9% episode growth, Texas LTACs strong. International India JV +18% on tourism, UK stable post-NHS renewals. Upside from Apollo synergies and rupee hedge.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the VitaHealth Partners Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
